question: The allotrope of which non-metal conducts electricity?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Carbon__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Graphite is a non-metal which is a good conductor of both heat and electricity.
 
• It is an allotrope of carbon, other allotropic forms being **diamond, amorphous carbon, etc**.
 
• The conductive properties of graphite come from its unique structure.
 
• It is composed of layers of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagon lattice.
 
• **These layers are weakly bonded so they can slide over one another, which is why graphite is also used as a lubricant.**
 
• **Furthermore, within these layers, each carbon atom is only bonded to three others.**
 
• This leaves one free electron, which can move within the layer.
 
• This mobility of electrons allows for the conduction of electricity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sulfur**

 
 
• **​**Sulfur is a **chemical element**; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
 
• It is** abundant, multivalent and nonmetallic. **
 
• **Under normal conditions, sulfur atoms form cyclic octatomic molecules with the chemical formula S₈. **
 
• **Elemental sulfur is a bright yellow, crystallin**e solid at room temperature.
 
 
 
• **Phosphorus:**
 
 
• Phosphorus is a non-metal, yet it does not conduct electricity or heat very well.
 
• Its atomic structure doesn't allow for the free movement of electrons which is essential for conductivity.
